title: After I Cross That Gate
style: Dream-pop ballad, 68 BPM slow sway; female alto with a light Flemish accent, breathy and close, rising into a powerful full-voice belt with layered octave doubles; male low baritone, tired and half-spoken in the verses. Their voices overlap without resolving in the final chorus. Shimmering reverb guitars and slow-washed synth pads sit against wipers, city rain, and a distant airport chime in the bridge; soft brushed drums and round sub bass carry the tense pulse as E major drifts to C# minor.
lyrics:
[Intro]
[rain on a taxi window, wipers keeping time, reverb guitar]

[Verse 1]
[male:]
Calle 26, the wipers counting down,
your bag between our knees, the meter running,
the radio low, a bolero nobody's singing,
orange lights sliding over Bogotá.
[female:]
You keep your hands where I can see them,
like a man who's learned to leave no prints.
[male:]
I'm only saying what I want to say before it's gone.

[Pre-Chorus]
[male:]
Give me something real,
at least until you cross that gate.

[Chorus]
[female:]
It'll be real after I cross that gate,
when there's an ocean and nothing to prove,
when you can't drive me, can't wait, can't save me,
and you still pick up the phone.
It's not a romance, it's not a goodbye,
don't make it smaller than it is.
It'll be real after I cross that gate,
or it was never real at all.

[Verse 2]
[female:]
I came to fix the broken things in strangers,
I'm going home with one I couldn't fix.
[male:]
I never asked you to.
[female:]
You called me, John Amerikaan,
from a tienda, with your lip still wet.
[male:]
And you came.
[female:]
And I came.
That's the only promise either of us kept.

[Pre-Chorus]
[male:]
So give me something real,
at least until you cross that gate.

[Chorus]
[female:]
It'll be real after I cross that gate,
when there's an ocean and nothing to prove,
when you can't drive me, can't wait, can't save me,
and you still pick up the phone.
It's not a romance, it's not a goodbye,
don't make it smaller than it is.
It'll be real after I cross that gate,
or it was never real at all.

[Bridge]
[airport chime, a boarding call echoing]
[male:]
International departures, the white floor shining,
and there, by the counter, a girl with a backpack,
her father's hand on her shoulder, Müller,
his eyes going over the hall like mine do.
[female:]
You're gone already. I can feel you counting exits.
[male:]
He's right there.
[female:]
Please… forget about him.
Just tonight.
I'm the one who's leaving.
Look at me.

[Final Chorus]
[female:]
It'll be real after I cross that gate,
[male:]
give me something real,
[female:]
when there's an ocean and nothing to prove,
[male:]
until you cross that gate,
[female:]
when you can't drive me, can't wait, can't save me,
[male:]
and I still pick up the phone.
[female:]
It's not a romance,
[male:]
it's not a goodbye,
[female:]
don't make it smaller than it is.
[male:]
It'll be real after you cross that gate,
[female:]
or it was never real at all.

[Outro]
[reverb guitar alone, rain fading into terminal hum]
[female:]
Tot later, John.
[male:]
Tot later.
[End]
